Assume the model graph and tensor shapes, parameter/activation sizes, precision, GPU count and usable HBM (GiB), measured interconnect bandwidth/latency, software versions, clock state, request-length and arrival distributions, concurrency, batching policy, and latency, throughput, error, quality, and availability SLOs are known. Label measurements separately from estimates. First enumerate topology-compatible tensor-parallel degrees and pipeline stage partitions, rejecting any plan without positive per-GPU HBM headroom, correct placement, and a safe reconfiguration path. TP may reduce per-stage memory pressure through sharding but pays synchronized collectives on the critical path; PP can limit collectives but pays activation transfers, stage imbalance, bubbles, and possible queueing. For a latency-sensitive service, use the smallest feasible microbatch (often one request or a deliberately specified microbatch), and do not infer a training-oriented batch-size conclusion: measure batching and synchronization behavior under the real request mix. Hypothesis: with hardware, model, precision, software, clocks, concurrency, arrival rate, batching, and workload strata held constant, the candidate that has lower held-out end-to-end p99 latency while meeting every pre-registered SLO gate will outperform the alternative; the hypothesis is falsified if the p99 ordering reverses, its confidence interval overlaps the decision margin, or any memory, error, quality, or availability gate fails. Warm up both candidates, randomize assignment and trial order, tune only on a disjoint set, then evaluate on held-out requests across load and sequence-length strata with repeated runs. Measure end-to-end p50/p95/p99 latency in ms, queueing, compute, collective and activation-transfer time, per-GPU HBM GiB and headroom, utilization, synchronization waits, stage imbalance/bubble time, throughput, error/retry rate, quality, and recovery time; report sample counts, uncertainty, and saturation points. Control for thermal throttling, placement, background load, cache state, request mix, batching, and autoscaling, and log rejected trials. Compare failure and reconfiguration costs using only authorized, isolated tests: drain traffic, preserve health checks and observability, verify correctness, canary the winner, and retain the previous configuration. Roll back on SLO breach, elevated errors, quality regression, unsafe HBM, missing telemetry, failed health checks, or unrecoverable worker/stage loss. Measure end-to-end p50/p95/p99 latency in ms, queueing, compute, collective and activation-transfer time, per-GPU HBM GiB and headroom, utilization, synchronization waits, stage imbalance/bubble time, throughput, error/retry rate, quality, and recovery time; report sample counts, uncertainty, and saturation points. Control for thermal throttling, placement, background load, cache state, request mix, batching, and autoscaling, and log rejected trials. Compare failure and reconfiguration costs using only authorized, isolated tests: drain traffic, preserve health checks and observability, verify correctness, canary the winner, and retain the previous configuration. Roll back on SLO breach, elevated errors, quality regression, unsafe HBM, missing telemetry, failed health checks, or unrecoverable worker/stage loss. Platform-specific facts, thresholds, and a universal winner require evidence and domain review.
risks: Platform facts and SLO thresholds are unspecified; no universal TP/PP choice is justified.
Tail latency may be dominated by queueing, batching, collectives, stage imbalance, stragglers, retries, or workload drift.
Failure injection and reconfiguration can affect service unless explicitly authorized and isolated.
evidence_required: Measured HBM headroom, topology, communication, and balanced stage feasibility for each candidate.
Randomized paired trials with disjoint tuning and held-out latency, throughput, error, quality, and availability results stratified by workload and load.
Pre-registered SLO gates plus authorized isolated canary, failure/recovery, monitoring, and rollback records.
